newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa extends amnesty for human rights abusers.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa extends amnesty for human rights abusers.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela announced on Friday he had agreed to extend by five months the deadline for amnesty applications under a post- apartheid reconciliation programme.

Apartheid's foes and defenders had been given until midnight on Saturday to apply for amnesty for crimes committed with a political motive, but Mandela told a news conference offenders would now be allowed to apply by May 10, 1997.
The president said in a statement read on his behalf by spokesman Joel Netshitenzhe that he had also agreed to set May 10, 1994, as the cut-off date for abuses that could qualify for amnesty.

"...I have in the past week listened carefully to Bishop Desmond Tutu and General Constand Viljoen and reflected intensely on their arguments," he said in the statement after talks with officials of Tutu's "truth commission", which has to consider the pardons, and white conservative Freedom Front leader Viljoen.
Tutu had argued for the cut-off date of December 5, 1993 to be extended to May 10, 1994 -- the date of Mandela's inauguration as South Africa's first democratically elected president.

Viljoen also asked for the cut-off date to be moved so that amnesty could be considered for right-wingers who carried out a bombing spree in the run-up to the April 1994 all-race elections and others who plotted a coup at the time to derail democracy.
